The stencil master's own outline, which has no ears (a half-width box), is 221.25 x 43.79 and agrees to a quarter of a millimetre; the chassis carries the data sheet's figures. \"19' rack and wall-mounting options\" (2019 edition) - the brackets are not part of the face."},"eth-speed":{"confidence":"borrowed","note":"BORROWED, NOT STATED. The data sheets list \"1 x Console RJ45 port\" and are silent on the ETH management port's rate. 1g is taken from the TM-8104's OOB port on the maintainer's ruling for unstated management rates; the eth-speed gap stays open."},"front-layout":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"POSITIONS ARE THIS BOX'S OWN RENDER, SHAPES THE STENCIL'S. The 2025 render (telco.com 2025/09/TMC3312SC.png) is rectified by a four-corner homography onto the data sheet's 221 x 44 (corners TL 170.5,186.5 TR 671,186.5 BR 670,280 BL 171,280; about 2.3 px/mm, so good to about a millimetre) and every jack, cage, lamp, slot and vent is placed where it lands. The NetZoom master TMC-3312SC (F) was the first source used and is retired for positions: it puts the copper jacks on a 16.7 pitch where this render measures 14.3, and the TM-3348's render (the same left half at 5.4 px/mm) measures 14.1; its blocks sit 0.5-4 mm from where both renders put them, not at a constant offset. The two renders agree with each other on the shared left half to about 0.2 mm once each image's corner offset is removed. The stencil keeps its legends and the cage and jack shapes."},"jack-lamps":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"The 2025 render shows lamp windows on the CON console and on all eight CES jacks (the CES jacks' red and green corners, and the STS / FLT legends printed under CON naming its two). None of the nine is Ethernet, so each is the bare std/rj45-ganged@2 with its two windows placed beside it as common/led-rect-sm@1, for: the jack, at the corners where common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 draws its own."},"lamps":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"SYNC, SD, PS1 and PS2 are about 4 mm lamps with a pinhole between SD and PS1, placed where the rectified render has them, as are the wordmark plate, the four short slots under the model name and the vent dashes along the top edge (none of which the stencil draws); LNK/ACT and MNG are printed over the ETH jack and STS and FLT under the CON jack, naming those jacks' own lamp windows. No document says what any state means."},"model":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"TM-3312 data sheet (telco.com 2026/08), \"Ethernet/MPLS/IP and TDM CES Multi-Service NID\"; the 2019 and 2021 editions call it the T-Marc 3312SC/SCH, and the face prints TMC-3312SC."},"ports":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"Copper 1/1-1/4 (columns 65.15 and 79.4) and CES 3/1-3/8 (columns 159.85, 175.45, 191.1 and 206.6) are 2 x 2 RJ45 blocks with lamp windows in their outer corners - the render shows them on every jack. Copper is common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, upper row turned 180; the CES jacks carry T1/E1, not Ethernet, so they are the bare std/rj45-ganged@2 with their two lamp windows placed as common/led-rect-sm@1 where the lamped part draws its own - the family's way of drawing a lamped non-Ethernet jack (juniper/mx204's BITS). The data sheet calls the CES jacks RJ-45; rj48 is the library's media name for a T1/E1 jack. SFP 2/1-2/8 are a 2 x 4 stacked block on a 14.3 pitch (columns 98.4-141.3) with TWO arrow lamps per port in the strip between the rows: the render prints \u25bc\u25b2\u25bc\u25b2 across each column, at -4.75, -1.9, +1.8 and +4.65 mm from the column centre (the TM-3348's render gives the same offsets); what the pair means is undocumented. Numbering as printed: odd above, even below in every block."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"\"2 x internal AC power supplies\" (TMC-3312SC-2AC-x) or \"2 x internal DC wide-range (-24 VDC to -72 VDC)\" (TMC-3312SC-2DC, TMC-3312SH-2DC); \"redundant AC/DC power supply\". No consumption figure is published. The supplies are internal, so the front carries no bays; their inlets are presumably at the rear."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Three data-sheet editions (2019-01, 2021-05, 2026-08), three vendor renders of which telco.com 2025/09/TMC3312SC.png (858 px) is the best, and the legacy NetZoom stencil \"Telco Systems\" (2022), master TMC-3312SC (F).
